semantic_units.independent_assessment: The original EN/KR asks concrete impacts of TR38.824 on both TS38.211 and38.214. The original five output roles are study, TS, impact type, affected sections and detailed description. The proposed repair preserves all five aliases, both TSs, and the source-certified existing-section extension role. It replaces the generic manual section5 description with retained implementation components. No additional output identity or approval-vote field is required.

The study is selected through its original TR identity and study-WI edge. Original study conclusions9.1/9.2 and official study800095/Core830174/parent830074 plus TR21.916 section5.2 certify this FS-to-Core family bridge. The implementation program draws on both TR38.824 and38.825, so the answer is implementation lineage associated with the named study, without an exclusive-causality claim. Both requested TS selectors remain exact.

Agreed CRs supply implementation witnesses in the certified family. Single-WI covers bind their reason/summary as source context; mixed covers contribute explicit URLLC-topic or matching-WI-header paragraphs. I inspected the actual selected mixed components and complete candidate frontier. The query supplies no handpicked CR-ID list, source annotations or new source-body runtime content. The bounded selection does not equate every family CR or every URLLC mention with a study effect. Mixed section roles require the selected paragraph to mention the retained section number.

The answer unit remains one descriptive record for each requested TS. Distinct incident WorkItem codes prevent duplicate-carrier joins, and section identifiers are deduplicated. Every selected reason/summary component is serialized with its retained CR identifier/property context; duplicates caused by real mirrored CR records remain genuine distinct source witnesses. The query aggregates per TS rather than returning a CR-count surrogate.

Both TSs have concrete substantive details:211 extends DMRS with DCI0_2/1_2 and includes TypeB channel-inference and interleaver changes;214 supplies resource allocation, repetition/segmentation, configured grants, DMRS/PT-RS, hopping and related refinements. The two full records contain35 carriers/74 paragraphs,812 and28278 description characters, without output sampling. The original question requests detail, not an exhaustive catalogue of every historical carrier or every normative clause; no new exhaustive-history gate is imposed. Omitted mixed paragraphs are not classified as no effect.

The original spec-number ascending order is preserved. Stable internal CR-ID/property and lexically sorted section serialization produce deterministic descriptive records. This imposes no new ranking or tie convention on the question. Sequence/cardinality contracts will use the existing released scorer schema.
